On the morning ward round she cannot be roused and does not respond to voice. Her capillary glucose is 1.9 mmol/L. She has a working intravenous cannula in her forearm.

What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN1245.correct_answer: Give intravenous glucose through the cannula

For several days, a 44-year-old woman has severe vertigo that came on suddenly; there is no accompanying hearing loss or tinnitus. Which diagnosis fits best?
A 66-year-old woman on digoxin for atrial fibrillation is found to have a sudden deterioration in renal function on routine bloods. Why does this finding prompt an urgent medication review?
UN1451.correct_answer: Reduced clearance can cause digoxin accumulation and toxicity

UN1499.presentation: Coughing on Swallowing After a Stroke
UN1499.stem: Two days after an ischaemic stroke, a patient coughs repeatedly every time they are given water to drink. What complication should be suspected?

A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN1499.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN1499.stem: Care home staff ask the visiting GP about an 82-year-old woman with advanced Alzheimer's disease. At mealtimes she holds food in her mouth for long periods, coughs while eating and drinking, and her voice sounds wet afterwards. Her weight is stable and she is not currently unwell. Which complication is she most at risk of?

A 6-year-old boy is brought to his GP with very red cheeks for two days, as though he had been slapped, and now a faint lace-like rash on his arms and thighs. He had a mild cold last week and is well in himself. His mother is 16 weeks pregnant, and his aunt, who often looks after him, has sickle cell disease.

What is the most likely cause, and what is the key concern?
UN1499.correct_answer: Parvovirus B19 — risk to the pregnancy and to people with haemolytic anaemia

UN1499.presentation: Cavitating lesion in a smoker — next imaging
UN1499.stem: A 63-year-old man who smokes 20 cigarettes a day is admitted to the medical ward after four weeks of fever, cough and weight loss. He has no history of alcohol misuse, seizures, dental disease or swallowing problems. A chest X-ray shows a cavitating lesion with an air-fluid level in the right upper lobe. Which imaging is most appropriate next to characterise the lesion and look for an underlying cause?
A 2-year-old boy suddenly starts coughing forcefully and develops a wheeze heard only over the right side of his chest while he is eating grapes. What is the most likely cause?
An 80-year-old develops a hot, acutely swollen knee. Aspiration of the joint fluid reveals calcium pyrophosphate crystals under polarised light microscopy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 69-year-old man with motor neurone disease attends the neurology clinic with his wife. She says that over recent weeks he splutters when drinking tea and that his voice becomes gurgly afterwards. His speech has also become slurred. He has no limb swelling, ear pain, loin pain or headache. Which complication is he most at risk of?

UN1502.stem: An older person with multiple long-term conditions, reduced mobility and recurrent admissions is identified as frail. What is the most appropriate overall management approach?
An 82-year-old woman is admitted with a displaced intracapsular hip fracture. She is medically stable. What is the most appropriate principle regarding surgery?
UN1502.correct_answer: Operate within 36 hours (day of or day after admission) once optimised

UN1502.stem: A patient with stable but symptomatic COPD remains breathless on minimal exertion despite being on maximal appropriate inhaled therapy. Which non-drug intervention would most improve his exercise capacity and quality of life?

UN1502.presentation: Coughing on Swallowing After a Stroke
UN1502.stem: Two days after an ischaemic stroke, a patient coughs repeatedly every time they are given water to drink. What complication should be suspected?

An 81-year-old widow who lived alone and did her own shopping is recovering on a medical ward after treatment for pneumonia. Nurses report that she now needs help from two staff to wash and dress and cannot make herself a drink. Her son asks whether she should go straight into a nursing home. What is the most appropriate approach?
UN1502.correct_answer: Assess her functional needs and rehabilitation potential with the multidisciplinary team

UN1502.stem: A 70-year-old man suffers a stroke affecting the left occipital lobe. Afterwards, he has lost the same side of the visual field — the right side — in both eyes. What is this visual deficit called?

A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

A 76-year-old Black woman is on a rehabilitation unit after a stroke. During a skin check, the nurse notices that a well-defined area over her sacrum looks darker and purplish compared with the surrounding skin. It feels warmer and slightly firmer, the skin is unbroken, and the area does not lighten when pressed. What does this most likely indicate?

UN1545.stem: An overweight young woman has headaches, transient visual obscurations and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows papilloedema, but neurological examination is otherwise normal and brain imaging shows no mass or hydrocephalus. Lumbar puncture shows a raised opening pressure with normal constituents. What is the diagnosis?

UN1545.presentation: Papilloedema with suspected IIH — image before lumbar puncture
UN1545.stem:
A 30-year-old woman is referred to the acute medical unit by her optometrist, who saw swelling of both optic discs at a routine eye test. For a month she has had a daily headache that is worse when she lies down and when she coughs. She has gained weight over the past year and is otherwise well, with no fever, neck stiffness or focal neurological signs. The medical registrar suspects idiopathic intracranial hypertension (raised brain pressure with no identifiable cause) and suggests a lumbar puncture this afternoon to measure the opening pressure. No brain imaging has been done.

What should be the next investigation?

A 27-year-old woman in the emergency department has fever, neck stiffness and photophobia. She is alert, orientated and asking sensible questions. The registrar plans an urgent diagnostic lumbar puncture, and a junior doctor is asked to prepare her.

What must happen before the needle is inserted?
UN1545.correct_answer: Explain its purpose, what it involves, its risks and alternatives, then get her consent

UN1545.stem: A 28-year-old obese woman has daily headaches that are worse in the morning and on lying down, with brief episodes of visual blurring and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT of the head is normal. Lumbar puncture shows a markedly raised opening pressure with normal CSF constituents. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old obese woman presents with a 6-week history of daily headache worse on lying down and on coughing, with transient visual obscurations. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN1545.correct_answer: Lumbar puncture with measurement of opening pressure

UN1545.presentation: Idiopathic intracranial hypertension — first-line drug treatment
UN1545.stem: A 27-year-old woman with a body mass index of 36 kg/m² has been diagnosed with idiopathic intracranial hypertension after MRI with venography and lumbar puncture. She has daily headaches and bilateral papilloedema, but her visual acuity and visual fields are normal. She is not pregnant and is using reliable contraception. She has been referred to a weight management programme. Which drug is most appropriate to add?

A 55-year-old has several weeks of headaches that are worse in the early morning and on lying down, coughing or straining, with associated vomiting. Fundoscopy reveals papilloedema, and there is a new subtle focal neurological deficit. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN1545.presentation: Child with headache, vomiting and double vision
UN1545.stem:
An 8-year-old girl has had headaches for three weeks. They are worst on waking and she has been vomiting before breakfast. Her mother has now noticed that she sees double and tilts her head when reading. She has no fever, no neck stiffness and no history of head injury.

What is the most appropriate approach?
UN1545.correct_answer: Urgent paediatric assessment for possible raised intracranial pressure

UN1679.stem: A 60-year-old woman has brief episodes of rotational vertigo lasting under a minute, triggered by rolling over in bed or looking up. The Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre reproduces transient vertigo with rotatory nystagmus. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A 74-year-old woman has been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease by a specialist. Over the past year her handwriting has become small, she has a tremor of her left hand at rest, and she now takes a long time to dress and has difficulty turning over in bed. Examination shows asymmetrical rigidity and slow, small movements. She lives alone and wants treatment to stay independent. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
UN1679.correct_answer: Levodopa combined with a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor

UN1679.stem: A 7-year-old girl is brought to her GP because her teacher has noticed that she switches off many times a day, sometimes in the middle of a sentence, with her eyelids fluttering. Each episode lasts only seconds, she does not fall, and she carries on with her task straight afterwards with no drowsiness. An episode is triggered in clinic when she is asked to breathe deeply and quickly for a few minutes. What kind of seizure is she most likely having?

A 19-year-old man of Armenian descent has had episodes of fever up to 39.5°C with severe abdominal pain since childhood. Each episode lasts 1 to 3 days and settles without treatment. During one attack he had a laparoscopy, which was normal apart from a small amount of sterile peritoneal fluid. Between attacks he is entirely well and his CRP returns to normal. His parents are first cousins and his younger sister has similar episodes, sometimes with a hot, swollen ankle. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 20-month-old boy is brought to the GP by his mother after an episode yesterday. He banged his head on a table, gave a short cry, then went very pale and limp, stiffened with a few jerks, and was unresponsive for less than a minute. He was back to his usual self within a couple of minutes. A similar episode happened two months ago after a fall. He is developing normally and examination, including the heart, is normal.

What is the most appropriate management?
UN1679.correct_answer: Explain that these are benign reflex anoxic seizures and reassure

UN1679.stem: A 34-year-old man's wife describes episodes that occur a few times a month. He first says he has a strange rising feeling in his stomach, then stares blankly, does not respond to her, chews repeatedly and fiddles with his shirt buttons. Each episode lasts around ninety seconds, after which he is muddled for a short time and cannot remember what happened. He has never fallen or jerked. Which seizure type best describes these episodes?

A 77-year-old man with Parkinson's disease tells his GP that whenever he gets out of bed or rises from his armchair, his vision greys out and he feels he might faint. The symptoms settle within a minute if he sits back down. He has no spinning sensation and no chest pain. Lying and standing blood pressures show a marked fall in systolic pressure after three minutes of standing, which reproduces his symptoms. What is the likeliest cause of his symptoms?

A 76-year-old woman attends her GP surgery because for the past month she has felt faint within seconds of getting up from her armchair, which settles if she sits back down. Over recent months amlodipine, ramipril and indapamide have been added to her treatment. Lying and standing blood pressure readings show a substantial drop on standing that reproduces her symptoms. She has no spinning sensation and no symptoms on turning her head. What is the most likely explanation?
UN1679.correct_answer: Orthostatic hypotension caused by her antihypertensive treatment

UN1681.presentation: Sudden Vertigo With Inability to Stand
UN1681.stem: A 59-year-old man develops sudden severe vertigo, is unable to stand or walk unsupported, and is found to have limb incoordination and nystagmus on examination. Which neurological structure should be particularly suspected?
For several days, a 44-year-old woman has severe vertigo that came on suddenly; there is no accompanying hearing loss or tinnitus. Which diagnosis fits best?

UN1681.presentation: Posterior Circulation Stroke vs Vestibular Neuritis
UN1681.stem: A 65-year-old man with hypertension and diabetes has sudden vertigo, vomiting and left-sided limb ataxia. He cannot sit unsupported. Head-impulse testing is normal and he has direction-changing nystagmus. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN1681.correct_answer: Urgent MRI brain with diffusion-weighted imaging

UN1681.stem: A 67-year-old man develops sudden left-sided facial droop. On examination he can wrinkle his forehead symmetrically, but the lower half of the left face is weak. He also has mild left arm weakness. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

A 63-year-old man speaks to his GP by telephone. For a week, every time he looks up to reach a high shelf or lies back on his pillow, the room spins violently for less than a minute and then settles. Between attacks he feels completely normal. He has no hearing loss, tinnitus, headache, weakness or difficulty speaking. At a face-to-face review the following day, the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre to the right reproduces his vertigo with a burst of torsional nystagmus after a short delay. Which condition is responsible?

A 38-year-old man develops sudden severe spinning vertigo with nausea after a recent cold. It has lasted two days. He also reports muffled hearing and ringing in his left ear since the onset, and has never had a similar episode. He has no vascular risk factors, limb weakness, speech disturbance or double vision, and examination shows horizontal nystagmus.

Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 70-year-old man with atrial fibrillation presents with a sudden onset of a painful, pale, cold and pulseless right leg with reduced sensation over the past 4 hours. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN1681.correct_answer: Urgent vascular surgical referral and IV heparin

UN1681.stem: A 60-year-old woman has brief episodes of rotational vertigo lasting under a minute, triggered by rolling over in bed or looking up. The Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre reproduces transient vertigo with rotatory nystagmus. What is the most appropriate treatment?

UN1684.stem: A 65-year-old man is found to have progressively enlarging optic disc cupping and peripheral visual field loss over several years. Which structure is being damaged in this chronic process?

A 6-month-old infant is brought to A&E. The parents report the baby rolled off the sofa 2 days ago. CT head shows bilateral subdural haemorrhages. Ophthalmological examination reveals bilateral retinal haemorrhages. There are no external bruises. What is the most likely diagnosis and next step?
UN1684.correct_answer: Abusive head trauma — immediate safeguarding referral and admission

UN1684.stem: A 51-year-old woman wakes unable to extend her wrist or fingers after falling asleep with her arm pressed against a hard edge for several hours. Which nerve is most likely injured?

A 33-year-old man twisted his left knee while turning sharply on a planted foot during a five-a-side match. He was able to finish the game, but the knee swelled gradually overnight. Over the following weeks it has intermittently locked, so that he cannot straighten it fully until he wiggles it free. There is tenderness along the medial joint line, a small effusion, and pain with a click on rotating the flexed knee. The Lachman test is normal. Which structure is most likely injured?

A cyclist falls onto the handlebars and CT shows a fracture through the floor of the right orbit. He has numbness of the lower eyelid, the side of the nose and the upper lip on that side.

Which nerve is most likely to have been injured?

A 54-year-old man reports 8 weeks of intermittent looser stools without rectal bleeding or weight loss. Examination is normal and he is not anaemic. According to current pathways, what is the most appropriate next step?
UN1684.correct_answer: Offer a faecal immunochemical test (FIT) to guide referral

UN1684.stem: A 19-year-old woman with no previous medical history is brought to the emergency department after a week of thirst, passing large amounts of urine and weight loss. Today she has vomited repeatedly, has abdominal pain and is drowsy, with deep, rapid breathing and a fruity smell on her breath. Her capillary glucose is very high, blood ketones are raised and a venous gas shows acidosis. Which diagnosis is most likely?
A 17-year-old girl has never had a period and has not developed any breast tissue. She also mentions that she has always had a poor sense of smell. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN1686.stem: A 67-year-old man develops sudden left-sided facial droop. On examination he can wrinkle his forehead symmetrically, but the lower half of the left face is weak. He also has mild left arm weakness. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

UN1686.presentation: Facial Weakness Affecting the Whole Side of the Face
UN1686.stem: A patient develops sudden weakness of the entire left side of the face, including the inability to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye. What type of facial nerve lesion does this represent?
UN1686.correct_answer: Lower motor neurone facial nerve palsy

UN1686.stem: Which of these symptoms most specifically points to involvement of the dominant cerebral hemisphere, in a patient with sudden facial weakness, arm weakness and difficulty speaking?

A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

A 38-year-old woman develops weakness affecting the entire left side of her face, including being unable to close her left eye and losing movement of her forehead on that side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1686.presentation: Facial Weakness That Spares the Forehead
UN1686.stem: A patient has weakness affecting only the lower part of the left side of the face, with normal, symmetrical forehead wrinkling on both sides. Which lesion best explains this finding?

UN1686.presentation: Unilateral Facial Weakness Including the Forehead
UN1686.stem: A patient wakes with weakness of the left side of the face, unable to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye, while the rest of their neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 70-year-old man develops sudden left arm weakness and slurred speech, which completely resolve within 30 minutes. CT brain shows no evidence of infarction. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN1695.stem: A 26-year-old woman develops progressive difficulty walking upstairs over several days, two weeks after an episode of diarrhoea. On examination she has symmetrical weakness in both legs with absent reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 30-year-old man develops progressive, symmetrical ascending leg weakness over 5 days, 2 weeks after a diarrhoeal illness. Reflexes are absent. CSF shows raised protein with a normal cell count. What is the most appropriate treatment, alongside monitoring of respiratory function?
A 52-year-old man with Guillain-Barré syndrome has weakness that is now extending to his arms. He is admitted for close monitoring. Which parameter best predicts impending respiratory failure?

A 45-year-old man presents with progressive ascending weakness of both legs over 4 days, now reaching the lower trunk. There is areflexia, and he had a diarrhoeal illness 2 weeks ago. Sensation is intact. Which investigation will best confirm the diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman develops progressively worsening weakness that starts in her feet and spreads upward, with loss of reflexes, about two weeks after a bout of diarrhoeal illness. Which diagnosis is most likely?

A 25-year-old man develops ascending weakness over a week, starting in his legs, with loss of reflexes and mild distal numbness. He had diarrhoea three weeks ago. What is the most important investigation to monitor in the acute phase?

A 45-year-old woman presents with a 3-day history of ascending symmetrical weakness starting in her feet. She now has difficulty standing and has mild facial weakness. Her deep tendon reflexes are absent. She has no respiratory distress, but you perform spirometry. The forced vital capacity (FVC) is 1.2 L (predicted normal 3.2 L). What is the single most appropriate immediate next step?
UN1695.correct_answer: Urgent ITU/HDU referral for monitoring and preparation for potential ventilatory support

UN1695.stem: A 46-year-old woman is admitted with 5 days of tingling in her feet and increasing weakness, first in her legs and now in her arms. She had a flu-like illness 10 days ago. She now needs a walking frame. Reflexes are absent in all four limbs and she has mild bilateral facial weakness. Forced vital capacity is being monitored and is currently stable. Lumbar puncture shows a raised protein with a normal white cell count. What is the most appropriate treatment?

UN1697.stem: A 37-year-old electrician collapsed at work, and colleagues describe about a minute of rhythmic jerking of all his limbs followed by a period of confusion. He had slept normally, drinks little alcohol and takes no regular medicines. At the first seizure clinic his examination is normal, and both his brain MRI and EEG show no abnormality. There is no family history of epilepsy. Which management is best?
UN1697.correct_answer: Give safety and driving advice without starting antiseizure medication

UN1697.presentation: Transient loss of consciousness — ECG finding needing specialist assessment
UN1697.stem: A 23-year-old woman is seen in the emergency department after briefly losing consciousness while standing in a queue. She felt hot and light-headed beforehand and recovered fully within a minute. Her examination is normal. Her 12-lead ECG is reviewed before discharge. Which ECG finding would mean she needs an urgent referral for cardiovascular assessment?
UN1697.correct_answer: Short PR interval with a delta wave

UN1697.stem: A 25-year-old woman has a first generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting about 90 seconds, witnessed by her partner, with full recovery afterwards. She has a family history of epilepsy. Neurological examination and capillary glucose are normal, and there is no head injury. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 40-year-old man with known epilepsy is brought to the emergency department with continuous generalised tonic-clonic seizure activity. He has now been convulsing for 25 minutes and has not regained consciousness between seizures. Intravenous access is established and he has already received two doses of intravenous lorazepam 10 minutes apart, which have not terminated the seizure. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 2-year-6-month-old boy is brought to the paediatric emergency department after a generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting 3 minutes during a febrile illness. He had one similar brief febrile seizure at 20 months and has no other neurological history. He recovered fully within 10 minutes. His temperature is 38.9°C and the left tympanic membrane is red and bulging. On review by the paediatric registrar he is alert and playing, with no signs of meningitis and a normal neurological examination. His parents feel confident to care for him at home. What is the most appropriate management?
UN1697.correct_answer: Observe for 1–2 hours and discharge with safety-netting

UN1697.stem: A 52-year-old man was admitted 20 hours ago with cellulitis. He drinks about 120 units of alcohol a week, but this was not recorded on admission and no alcohol withdrawal treatment has been started. He has a generalised tonic–clonic seizure lasting 2 minutes that stops on its own. Afterwards he is tremulous and sweaty but orientated. His capillary glucose is 6.1 mmol/L and he has no head injury. Which medicine is most appropriate to reduce the likelihood of further seizures?

A 32-year-old woman describes recurrent episodes that begin with zigzag lines and flashing lights in her vision lasting about 20 minutes. These are followed within an hour by a throbbing right-sided headache with nausea and sensitivity to light, lasting 4 to 6 hours. Between episodes she is well, and neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
Which feature in a patient presenting with a blackout should raise most concern for an underlying cardiac cause?
UN1697.correct_answer: Loss of consciousness that occurred while running

UN1720.presentation: Coughing on Swallowing After a Stroke
UN1720.stem: Two days after an ischaemic stroke, a patient coughs repeatedly every time they are given water to drink. What complication should be suspected?

A 68-year-old man develops a painful cluster of blistering lesions across the left side of his forehead and upper eyelid, sparing the tip of his nose. Which complication is particularly important to consider?

UN1720.presentation: Influenza Complication in an Older Adult
UN1720.stem: During a winter flu outbreak in her area, the family of an 81-year-old woman bring her in because she has suddenly spiked a temperature, developed a cough, and become muddled, which is completely out of character for her. Which complication is particularly important to consider in an older adult?

A 68-year-old man with confirmed vitamin B12 deficiency reports tingling and numbness in both feet, along with difficulty with balance when walking. Which complication is particularly important to recognise here?
UN1720.correct_answer: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord

UN1720.stem: A patient with a recent stroke and impaired swallowing develops a pneumonia, with consolidation seen in the right lower lobe. What is the most likely type of pneumonia and an important management consideration?
UN1720.correct_answer: Aspiration pneumonia — antibiotics and a swallow assessment

UN1720.stem: A 55-year-old woman receiving chemotherapy for breast cancer develops a temperature of 38.6°C. Her blood count shows a neutrophil count of 0.2 × 10⁹/L. What is the most important diagnosis to consider immediately?

Care home staff ask the visiting GP about an 82-year-old woman with advanced Alzheimer's disease. At mealtimes she holds food in her mouth for long periods, coughs while eating and drinking, and her voice sounds wet afterwards. Her weight is stable and she is not currently unwell. Which complication is she most at risk of?
A 3-year-old boy has a fever and a rash of small purple-red spots that do not fade when pressed. He is floppy and very difficult to wake. What is the most important diagnosis to consider?

UN1905.stem: A 58-year-old woman develops a tremor, generalised slowness of movement and difficulty starting to walk; her symptoms began predominantly on one side. Which feature is most characteristic of Parkinson's disease?

A 40-year-old woman has had nasal blockage, facial pressure and a reduced sense of smell continuously for the past four months, with no clear improvement. Which diagnosis is most consistent with this presentation?

A 68-year-old man with known Parkinson's disease finds it hard to get going when he starts walking, and his stride length shortens progressively as he continues. Which cardinal motor sign does this describe?

A 72-year-old man reports progressive slowness of movement over a year. He has an asymmetric resting tremor of the right hand and increasing stiffness, and his handwriting has become smaller. On examination there is cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, and a resting tremor that decreases when he reaches for an object. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A 72-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease has had several unexplained falls because she cannot correct her balance quickly enough when she is pushed off-centre. Which feature best explains this?

An older man has a slowly progressive, asymmetrical resting tremor ('pill-rolling'), rigidity (cogwheel) and bradykinesia, with a shuffling gait. He has no early falls and no eye-movement abnormality. What is the most likely diagnosis and most effective symptomatic treatment?
UN1905.correct_answer: Idiopathic Parkinson's disease — levodopa (with a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor)

UN1905.stem: A 72-year-old retired teacher is brought to his GP by his wife, who says his handwriting has become tiny and he now takes a long time to get dressed. He takes no regular medication. On examination his right hand shakes while resting in his lap but settles when he reaches for a pen. He has a reduced arm swing on the right when walking, and there is cogwheel stiffness at the right wrist. What is the likeliest diagnosis?
A 70-year-old man with known Parkinson's disease struggles to start walking and repeatedly freezes when approaching doorways. What term describes this symptom?

UN2181.stem: A 29-year-old woman with no past medical history comes in febrile, with a pounding headache, increasingly muddled, and has had several fits affecting one side of her body. Which diagnosis needs to be high on the list?

A 57-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department with rigors, a heart rate of 118/min and a blood pressure of 96/60 mmHg. She is being managed for suspected sepsis and blood cultures have been taken, but no obvious cause has been found yet.

Alongside starting treatment, what else is a priority in her assessment?
UN2181.correct_answer: Actively search for the source of infection

UN2181.presentation: Epilepsy — Drug Choice by Seizure Type
UN2181.stem: A 30-year-old man with newly diagnosed focal epilepsy needs a first-line antiepileptic. He has no contraindications. Which is an appropriate first-line choice for focal seizures?

A 23-year-old man describes recurrent episodes beginning with a rising sensation in the stomach and a feeling of déjà vu, followed by lip-smacking and plucking at his clothes, for which he is amnesic, lasting about a minute with brief postictal confusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN2181.correct_answer: Focal seizures of temporal lobe origin

UN2181.stem: A 54-year-old man with a mechanical aortic valve is referred to the acute medical unit by his GP after ten days of fevers, aches and fatigue. On arrival he is alert, his observations are stable and there is no obvious source of infection. The team suspects prosthetic valve endocarditis. Which investigation should be done before any antibiotic is given?
UN2181.correct_answer: Three sets of blood cultures from separate venepunctures

UN2181.presentation: Iron deficiency anaemia in an older man — next step
UN2181.stem: A 68-year-old man is found to have iron-deficiency anaemia with no obvious bleeding source on history. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN2181.correct_answer: Investigate the GI tract (upper and lower endoscopy)

UN2181.stem: A patient is hypotensive and tachycardic with a temperature of 38.9°C and a suspected source of infection. Which bundle of actions should be initiated urgently?
UN2181.correct_answer: The Sepsis Six within one hour

UN2181.presentation: Fever With Focal Bone Tenderness in a Child
UN2181.stem: A 7-year-old develops a fever and refuses to bear weight on one leg. On examination there is marked tenderness directly over the shaft of the tibia, with no joint swelling. What diagnosis should be suspected?

UN2278.presentation: Facial Weakness Affecting the Whole Side of the Face
UN2278.stem: A patient develops sudden weakness of the entire left side of the face, including the inability to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye. What type of facial nerve lesion does this represent?
UN2278.correct_answer: Lower motor neurone facial nerve palsy

UN2278.stem: A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

UN2278.presentation: Unilateral Facial Weakness Including the Forehead
UN2278.stem: A patient wakes with weakness of the left side of the face, unable to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye, while the rest of their neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 35-year-old man wakes with sudden unilateral facial droop. He cannot wrinkle his forehead on the affected side or fully close that eye, and there is no limb weakness or other deficit. What is the diagnosis and key treatment?
UN2278.correct_answer: Bell's palsy — give oral corticosteroids and protect the eye

UN2278.presentation: Mixed Upper And Lower Motor Neurone Signs
UN2278.stem: Visible wasting, fasciculations and brisk reflexes accompany progressively worsening weakness in both legs of a 64-year-old woman. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN2278.presentation: Facial Weakness That Spares the Forehead
UN2278.stem: A patient has weakness affecting only the lower part of the left side of the face, with normal, symmetrical forehead wrinkling on both sides. Which lesion best explains this finding?
A 60-year-old man has confirmed motor neurone disease with mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs and no sensory loss. Which drug is most likely to modestly prolong survival?

A 60-year-old man has progressive weakness with a mix of wasting and fasciculations (lower motor neuron) alongside brisk reflexes and up-going plantars (upper motor neuron), with no sensory loss and no eye-movement or sphincter involvement. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2283.stem: A patient with a long history of migraines now has a daily, near-constant headache. They have been taking analgesics (including codeine and triptans) on most days for months. What is the most likely cause and the key management step?
UN2283.correct_answer: Medication overuse headache — withdraw the overused analgesics

UN2283.stem: A 40-year-old woman has had a daily headache for several months. She has been taking combination analgesics containing codeine on 15 or more days each month, and her headaches have worsened despite escalating analgesia. Neurological examination is normal. What is the most appropriate management?

A 42-year-old woman with a long history of migraine sees her GP because her headaches have become daily over the last 6 months. She takes sumatriptan on about 15 days each month and paracetamol on most other days. She does not take opioids. Neurological and fundal examination are normal and there are no red-flag features. The GP diagnoses medication overuse headache. What is the most appropriate management?
UN2283.correct_answer: Stop the sumatriptan and paracetamol abruptly

UN2283.presentation: Chronic Daily Headache with Analgesic Overuse
UN2283.stem: Keeping a headache diary, a 52-year-old woman realises she has head pain on more than half the days of the month, and that she reaches for paracetamol or ibuprofen almost every time it occurs. What is driving the frequency of her headaches?

A 64-year-old woman tells her GP she has had frequent headaches and a ruddy, flushed complexion for several months. Repeated blood counts show her haemoglobin and haematocrit are consistently above the normal range, while her white cells and platelets are normal.

Which broad haematological diagnosis best describes her problem?

UN2283.presentation: Medically unexplained symptoms — new red-flag symptom
UN2283.stem: A 58-year-old woman has a long history of persistent physical symptoms, including abdominal discomfort, fatigue and headaches, for which thorough investigation has found no cause. She is managed with regular planned reviews with one GP. At today's review she reports that over the past 6 weeks her bowels have become persistently looser and more frequent and she has lost 4 kg without trying. Abdominal examination is normal. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN2283.correct_answer: Offer a quantitative faecal immunochemical test

UN2283.stem: A 27-year-old man with stable schizophrenia recently stopped his antipsychotic medication, and his family now notices he has become more suspicious and withdrawn. What is the most likely explanation?

A 66-year-old woman who went through the menopause fifteen years ago sees her GP because of tiredness. Her stools have been looser and more frequent for two months and her clothes have become loose. Blood tests show a microcytic anaemia with low ferritin. She eats a normal diet. Which diagnosis is most important to investigate for?

UN2289.stem: A 28-year-old woman presents with subacute painful loss of vision in one eye (optic neuritis). She recalls a separate episode of numbness and weakness in one leg, lasting two weeks, that fully resolved 18 months ago. MRI of the brain shows several scattered white-matter lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 28-year-old woman has had separate episodes over two years: painful loss of vision in one eye (optic neuritis) that recovered, and later a band of numbness ascending from the legs. MRI shows white-matter lesions disseminated in time and space. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 29-year-old woman presents with a 4-day history of painful loss of vision in the left eye with reduced colour vision and a relative afferent pupillary defect. She had a previous episode of limb numbness that resolved. MRI shows periventricular and optic nerve lesions. What is the most appropriate management of this acute episode?

UN2289.presentation: Recurrent Neurological Episodes In A Young Woman
UN2289.stem: A 27-year-old woman experiences an episode of painful visual loss in one eye, worse on eye movement, and recalls a previous episode of leg numbness that fully resolved. Which diagnosis should be considered?

UN2289.presentation: Neurological Episodes Separated in Time and Location
UN2289.stem: A 27-year-old woman had an episode of blurred vision in one eye six months ago that fully resolved, and now presents with new tingling and weakness in her right leg. Which diagnosis is most consistent?

A 70-year-old man with vascular risk factors has sudden, painless, complete loss of vision in one eye. Fundoscopy shows a pale retina with a cherry-red spot at the macula. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2289.presentation: Giant Cell Arteritis with Acute Visual Loss
UN2289.stem: A 75-year-old woman with biopsy-confirmed giant cell arteritis has been taking oral prednisolone 40 mg daily for 3 days. She now develops sudden, painless, complete loss of vision in her left eye. What is the most appropriate next step?
UN2289.correct_answer: Intravenous methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days

UN2289.presentation: Reduced Vision in One Eye Since Childhood
UN2289.stem: Vision screening in a 5-year-old picks up poor vision in the left eye only; a thorough eye examination finds nothing structurally wrong, and the problem is thought to stem from abnormal visual development during infancy. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2294.stem: A 64-year-old man has slowly worsening numbness and tingling that began in his feet and has spread upward, with diminished ankle reflexes. Which pattern is most consistent with a peripheral neuropathy?

A 59-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for 15 years attends her annual diabetes foot check. She says both feet tingle and feel numb, as though she is walking on cotton wool, and are worse at night. Ankle reflexes are absent on both sides and she cannot feel the monofilament on either sole. Muscle power in her legs is normal. Which pattern of nerve damage best fits?

A patient with type 2 diabetes has painful, burning, symmetrical numbness and tingling in both feet (a glove-and-stocking distribution) that disturbs sleep. Glycaemic control has been optimised. He also has coexisting low mood. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment for the neuropathic pain?
A 70-year-old man on long-term amiodarone for atrial fibrillation presents with unintentional weight loss, a fine tremor and palpitations. Which investigation is particularly relevant?
A 45-year-old man on long-term lithium for bipolar disorder reports persistent tiredness, unexplained weight gain and feeling cold all the time. Which investigation should be arranged?
An elderly woman on long-term metoclopramide develops symmetrical bradykinesia and rigidity with a mild tremor over a few weeks. What is the most likely cause, and the appropriate first action?
UN2294.correct_answer: Drug-induced parkinsonism — review and stop the offending drug

UN2294.stem: A 60-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes has burning, painful paraesthesiae in both feet in a 'stocking' distribution, worse at night. What is the most appropriate first-line drug for the neuropathic pain?

A 57-year-old taxi driver with type 2 diabetes has an HbA1c that has remained well above his agreed target for three years despite metformin and gliclazide. He feels well and asks the practice nurse why it matters if he has no symptoms.

Which long-term consequence of sustained hyperglycaemia is most important to explain?
UN2294.correct_answer: Damage to small vessels of the eyes, kidneys and nerves

UN2452.stem: An 82-year-old woman is on a stroke ward four days after a left hemisphere infarct. The nurse reports that she coughs immediately whenever she takes sips of water, food collects in her right cheek, and some fluid comes back through her nose. After drinking, her voice sounds gurgly. She does not report food sticking behind the breastbone. What type of swallowing problem is most likely?

A 74-year-old man reports a gradual onset of swallowing difficulty, describing that food occasionally 'goes down the wrong way', along with a new hoarse voice. Which feature points most strongly to an oropharyngeal rather than an oesophageal cause of his dysphagia?

UN2452.presentation: Coughing on Swallowing After a Stroke
UN2452.stem: Two days after an ischaemic stroke, a patient coughs repeatedly every time they are given water to drink. What complication should be suspected?

UN2452.presentation: Dysphagia — alarm feature for oesophageal cancer
UN2452.stem: A 70-year-old man presents with progressive difficulty swallowing solids over 4 months. He now struggles with soft food. He has lost 8 kg. What is the most appropriate next step?

A 77-year-old woman with Parkinson's disease is admitted to an acute medical ward after a fall. On the evening drug round, the nurse notices that she coughs and splutters each time she sips water to take her tablets, and her voice sounds gurgly afterwards. She is otherwise stable. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
UN2452.correct_answer: Stop oral intake and arrange a formal swallowing assessment

UN2452.stem: A 68-year-old man sees his GP because over the past six weeks pieces of meat and bread feel as though they hold up in the middle of his chest a few seconds after he swallows. He has no difficulty starting a swallow and does not cough or choke when eating. Swallowing is not painful, and between meals he feels nothing in his throat. How is his symptom best described?

UN2452.presentation: Dysphagia With Weight Loss And Anaemia
UN2452.stem: Blood tests reveal iron-deficiency anaemia in a 72-year-old woman who also describes worsening swallowing difficulty and losing weight without trying. Which diagnosis must be urgently excluded?

UN2452.presentation: Achalasia — dysphagia to solids and liquids
UN2452.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with intermittent difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. She describes food sticking in her chest. She has regurgitation of undigested food and occasional chest pain. She has lost 3 kg. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN2697.presentation: New Focal Seizure with Mass Lesion
UN2697.stem: Imaging confirms an intracranial mass in a 60-year-old woman, and she now has her first-ever seizure, limited to jerking of one hand. Which mechanism best explains why this localised fit has occurred?
UN2697.correct_answer: Abnormal discharge from cortex irritated by the lesion

UN2697.stem: A 23-year-old man describes recurrent episodes beginning with a rising sensation in the stomach and a feeling of déjà vu, followed by lip-smacking and plucking at his clothes, for which he is amnesic, lasting about a minute with brief postictal confusion. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN2697.correct_answer: Focal seizures of temporal lobe origin

UN2697.stem: A 34-year-old man's wife describes episodes that occur a few times a month. He first says he has a strange rising feeling in his stomach, then stares blankly, does not respond to her, chews repeatedly and fiddles with his shirt buttons. Each episode lasts around ninety seconds, after which he is muddled for a short time and cannot remember what happened. He has never fallen or jerked. Which seizure type best describes these episodes?

A 34-year-old woman has repeated episodes of wheeze and cough, especially at night and after exposure to house dust, with no symptoms in between episodes. Which feature of her history most supports a diagnosis of asthma?
UN2697.correct_answer: The variability of her respiratory symptoms

UN2697.stem: A 37-year-old electrician collapsed at work, and colleagues describe about a minute of rhythmic jerking of all his limbs followed by a period of confusion. He had slept normally, drinks little alcohol and takes no regular medicines. At the first seizure clinic his examination is normal, and both his brain MRI and EEG show no abnormality. There is no family history of epilepsy. Which management is best?
UN2697.correct_answer: Give safety and driving advice without starting antiseizure medication

UN2697.presentation: Recurrent Neurological Episodes In A Young Woman
UN2697.stem: A 27-year-old woman experiences an episode of painful visual loss in one eye, worse on eye movement, and recalls a previous episode of leg numbness that fully resolved. Which diagnosis should be considered?

A male baby is born at 40 weeks by emergency caesarean section for a placental abruption. He needs inflation breaths and chest compressions and his umbilical arterial pH shows a severe metabolic acidosis. At 2 hours of age on the local neonatal unit, which does not provide ongoing intensive care, he is lethargic and hypotonic with a weak suck, and has had a brief episode of rhythmic jerking of his right arm. He is now breathing spontaneously and his heart rate and blood pressure are stable. What is the most appropriate next step in management?
UN2697.correct_answer: Start therapeutic hypothermia and transfer to a cooling centre

UN2697.stem: A 30-year-old woman has episodes of low mood with suicidal thoughts. She also experiences auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions that persist even during periods when her mood is entirely normal. Her mood episodes have been present for most of her illness. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3140.stem: A 67-year-old man develops sudden left-sided facial droop. On examination he can wrinkle his forehead symmetrically, but the lower half of the left face is weak. He also has mild left arm weakness. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

A 38-year-old woman develops weakness affecting the entire left side of her face, including being unable to close her left eye and losing movement of her forehead on that side. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3140.presentation: Unilateral Facial Weakness Including the Forehead
UN3140.stem: A patient wakes with weakness of the left side of the face, unable to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye, while the rest of their neurological examination is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 71-year-old woman with long-standing hypertension and type 2 diabetes wakes with weakness of the left side of her face, her left arm and her left leg, all affected to a similar degree. Her speech content and understanding are normal, her visual fields are full and she has no neglect of the left side. Sensation is intact. Which type of stroke is most likely?

A 71-year-old woman has sudden left-sided weakness together with an upper motor neurone pattern of facial weakness on the right. Which cranial nerve is responsible for producing the facial weakness itself?

UN3140.presentation: Facial Weakness That Spares the Forehead
UN3140.stem: A patient has weakness affecting only the lower part of the left side of the face, with normal, symmetrical forehead wrinkling on both sides. Which lesion best explains this finding?

UN3140.presentation: Facial Weakness Affecting the Whole Side of the Face
UN3140.stem: A patient develops sudden weakness of the entire left side of the face, including the inability to raise the left eyebrow or fully close the left eye. What type of facial nerve lesion does this represent?
UN3140.correct_answer: Lower motor neurone facial nerve palsy

UN3140.stem: A 36-year-old woman who smokes and uses a combined hormonal pill for contraception is brought to the emergency department an hour after she suddenly dropped her cup and could not stand. She has weakness of the left arm and leg, a left facial droop and slurred speech. She has no history of migraine, and her capillary blood glucose is normal. What diagnosis must be urgently considered?

UN3211.stem: A 68-year-old man with confirmed vitamin B12 deficiency reports tingling and numbness in both feet, along with difficulty with balance when walking. Which complication is particularly important to recognise here?
UN3211.correct_answer: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord

UN3211.stem: A 55-year-old woman with pernicious anaemia stopped attending for her vitamin B12 injections two years ago. She now reports tingling in both feet and feeling unsteady when walking in the dark. On examination, vibration sense and joint position sense are reduced in both feet, ankle reflexes are absent and both plantar responses are extensor. Romberg's test is positive. Which condition is most likely?
UN3211.correct_answer: Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord

UN3211.presentation: Subacute Combined Degeneration of the Cord
UN3211.stem: A patient with low vitamin B12 develops a progressive unsteady gait, loss of vibration sense and proprioception in the feet, and weakness. Examination shows ABSENT ankle jerks but EXTENSOR (upgoing) plantar responses. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN3211.correct_answer: Subacute combined degeneration of the cord

UN3211.presentation: Suspected B12 deficiency with neurological signs — timing of treatment
UN3211.stem: A 68-year-old man is seen on the acute medical unit with 2 months of numbness in both feet, unsteadiness in the dark and falls. Vibration and joint position sense are impaired in the feet and Romberg's test is positive. Haemoglobin is 92 g/L with mean cell volume 118 fL. Vitamin B12 deficiency with spinal cord involvement is suspected. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3211.correct_answer: Send a B12 level, then start intramuscular B12 now

UN3211.presentation: Nitrous oxide-related vitamin B12 deficiency — initial test
UN3211.stem: A 20-year-old student presents to his GP with 3 weeks of numbness in both feet and an unsteady gait. He says he has inhaled large amounts of nitrous oxide from canisters most weekends for the past year. Romberg test is positive and vibration sense is reduced at the ankles. Vitamin B12 deficiency caused by nitrous oxide use is suspected. Which test should be used as the initial test for vitamin B12 deficiency?

A 66-year-old man with type 2 diabetes has taken metformin for 12 years. He has tingling in both feet. He eats a mixed diet including meat and dairy, has had no gastrointestinal surgery and has no other risk factors for vitamin B12 deficiency. Total vitamin B12 is low, haemoglobin is normal, and his GP judges metformin to be the cause. His diabetes is well controlled and metformin suits him. Which is the most appropriate treatment plan?
UN3211.correct_answer: Vitamin B12 replacement while continuing metformin

UN3211.stem: A 45-year-old woman with vitiligo and hypothyroidism tells her GP she has had pins and needles in both feet and hands for several months, along with tiredness and a sore, smooth red tongue. Her blood count shows a raised mean cell volume and her vitamin B12 level is low. Which examination finding is most likely?
UN3211.correct_answer: Reduced vibration sense in the feet with absent ankle jerks

UN3211.stem: A 27-year-old woman who has eaten a strict vegan diet for five years, without supplements, sees her GP with tiredness, a sore red smooth tongue and pins and needles in both feet. She looks pale with a slight lemon tinge. Blood tests show an anaemia with large red cells. She drinks no alcohol and her thyroid function is normal. Which deficiency is most likely?

UN3305.stem: A patient develops a foot drop after a period of prolonged leg crossing (or a tight plaster cast). There is weakness of ankle dorsiflexion and foot eversion with sensory loss over the dorsum of the foot, but ankle inversion, plantarflexion and the ankle jerk are preserved. Where is the lesion?
UN3305.correct_answer: The common peroneal (fibular) nerve at the fibular neck

UN3305.stem: A 51-year-old woman wakes unable to extend her wrist or fingers after falling asleep with her arm pressed against a hard edge for several hours. Which nerve is most likely injured?

UN3305.presentation: Foot drop — L5 radiculopathy vs common peroneal palsy
UN3305.stem:
A 58-year-old man has had three weeks of his left foot slapping on the ground when he walks. He has lost a lot of weight since weight-loss surgery six months ago and often sits with his legs crossed at his desk. He has also had intermittent aching in his lower back. Examination shows weak left ankle dorsiflexion and big toe extension, with reduced sensation over the dorsum of the left foot. The examining doctor wants to decide whether this is an L5 root lesion or a common peroneal nerve palsy at the fibular head.

Which additional examination finding would most strongly favour an L5 root lesion?

UN3305.presentation: Foot drop: L5 root versus peroneal nerve
UN3305.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had 3 weeks of right-sided low back pain radiating down the leg, and her right foot now 'slaps' on the floor when she walks. Examination shows weakness of ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension, and also weakness of ankle inversion and hip abduction. Sensation is reduced over the dorsum of the foot. Knee and ankle reflexes are preserved. There is no history of leg crossing, recent weight loss or a tight cast. What is the most likely site of the lesion?

A cyclist falls onto the handlebars and CT shows a fracture through the floor of the right orbit. He has numbness of the lower eyelid, the side of the nose and the upper lip on that side.

Which nerve is most likely to have been injured?

A 25-year-old man presents with slowly progressive foot drop, high-arched feet (pes cavus) and hammer toes. His father has similar foot shape. He has weakness of foot dorsiflexion and absent ankle reflexes. Sensory loss is minimal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
UN3305.correct_answer: Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy)

UN3305.stem: A 50-year-old man has weight loss, fever, myalgia, abdominal pain, hypertension and a foot-drop (mononeuritis multiplex). He is hepatitis B surface antigen positive. Angiography shows microaneurysms in medium-sized arteries, and the lungs are spared. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A patient awakens with a 'wrist drop' (inability to extend the wrist and fingers) after falling asleep with their arm draped over a chair. Sensation is reduced over the dorsum of the hand near the base of the thumb. Which nerve is affected?
UN3305.correct_answer: The radial nerve (at the spiral groove of the humerus)

UN3317.stem: A patient with type 2 diabetes has painful, burning, symmetrical numbness and tingling in both feet (a glove-and-stocking distribution) that disturbs sleep. Glycaemic control has been optimised. He also has coexisting low mood. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment for the neuropathic pain?

A 59-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes for 15 years attends her annual diabetes foot check. She says both feet tingle and feel numb, as though she is walking on cotton wool, and are worse at night. Ankle reflexes are absent on both sides and she cannot feel the monofilament on either sole. Muscle power in her legs is normal. Which pattern of nerve damage best fits?

UN3317.presentation: Avoiding serotonin syndrome — neuropathic pain in a patient on citalopram
UN3317.stem: A 61-year-old man with type 2 diabetes sees his GP with burning pain in both feet that disturbs his sleep. Painful diabetic neuropathy is diagnosed. He has taken citalopram for depression for 3 years and his mood is stable on it. His renal function is normal. He would like a drug for the pain and wishes to stay on citalopram. Which drug is most appropriate to start?

A 64-year-old man has slowly worsening numbness and tingling that began in his feet and has spread upward, with diminished ankle reflexes. Which pattern is most consistent with a peripheral neuropathy?

A 60-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes has burning, painful paraesthesiae in both feet in a 'stocking' distribution, worse at night. What is the most appropriate first-line drug for the neuropathic pain?
A patient who has had type 1 diabetes for over 15 years is found on repeated testing to have persistently raised urinary albumin excretion. What complication is most likely developing?

A 57-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes attends her annual diabetic review. The nurse finds a painless, round ulcer surrounded by thick callus on the sole beneath the ball of her right big toe. She was unaware of it. She cannot feel the monofilament at several sites on either foot, but her feet are warm and the foot pulses are bounding. Which mechanism best explains the ulcer?
UN3317.correct_answer: Loss of protective sensation from peripheral neuropathy

UN3317.stem:
A 59-year-old man with type 1 diabetes and loss of feeling in both feet is seen in the diabetes clinic. He lives alone and asks what he should be doing at home to look after his feet.

What is the most important advice to give?
UN3317.correct_answer: Inspect his feet every day and protect them from injury

UN3345.presentation: Brain abscess — first imaging and avoiding lumbar puncture
UN3345.stem: A 46-year-old man is admitted with 5 days of worsening headache, fever and new right-sided weakness. Two weeks ago he was treated for a dental abscess. His temperature is 38.4°C, Glasgow Coma Scale score is 14 and there is mild right arm and leg weakness. A brain abscess is suspected and blood cultures have been taken. Which investigation should be performed next?
UN3345.correct_answer: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI of the brain

UN3345.stem: A man with advanced HIV (CD4 count 50 cells/µL) and poor treatment adherence presents with headache, fever and a focal neurological deficit. Contrast CT of the brain shows multiple RING-ENHANCING lesions. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 55-year-old has several weeks of headaches that are worse in the early morning and on lying down, coughing or straining, with associated vomiting. Fundoscopy reveals papilloedema, and there is a new subtle focal neurological deficit. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN3345.presentation: Acute otitis media complicated by mastoiditis — escalation
UN3345.stem: A 3-year-old girl is being managed at home for acute otitis media. Four days later her parents bring her back to the GP. She has a fever, and there is a red, tender, boggy swelling behind her left ear, which is pushed forwards and outwards. What is the most appropriate management?
UN3345.correct_answer: Same-day hospital referral for specialist assessment

UN3345.stem:
A 2-year-old boy is brought to the out-of-hours GP service by his father because he has been tugging at his right ear, crying and refusing food since last night. He had a runny nose and cough for the previous four days. His temperature is 38.6 °C. Otoscopy shows a red, opaque eardrum that is bulging, with loss of the light reflex. There is no swelling or tenderness behind the ear.

What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3345.presentation: Acute otitis media worsening on amoxicillin — second-choice antibiotic
UN3345.stem: A 3-year-old boy was diagnosed with acute otitis media 3 days ago and started on amoxicillin, which his parents confirm he has taken as prescribed. He has no drug allergies. His fever has continued and his ear pain is worse. He is alert and drinking, and there is no swelling or tenderness behind the ear, no neck stiffness and no other sign of serious illness. Otoscopy again shows a red, bulging right eardrum. Which antibiotic should be prescribed now?

A 52-year-old woman has a 1-week history of headache, fever and confusion following a severe sinus infection. Contrast-enhanced MRI shows a single 2 cm ring-enhancing lesion in the left frontal lobe with surrounding oedema. Blood cultures have been taken and the neurosurgical team will review her today. She has no drug allergies. Which empirical antibiotic regimen is most appropriate?

UN3345.presentation: Chronic Ear Fluid And Hearing Loss
UN3345.stem: A 4-year-old boy has frequent ear infections and his parents feel he is not hearing well. On examination the eardrum looks dull with fluid visible behind it, but there is no sign of acute inflammation. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3346.stem: A 50-year-old man with a known brain tumour reports headache and vomiting, and fundoscopy shows swollen, blurred optic discs bilaterally. What does this finding, papilloedema, indicate in this context?

A 55-year-old has several weeks of headaches that are worse in the early morning and on lying down, coughing or straining, with associated vomiting. Fundoscopy reveals papilloedema, and there is a new subtle focal neurological deficit. What is the most appropriate next investigation?

UN3346.presentation: Child with headache, vomiting and double vision
UN3346.stem:
An 8-year-old girl has had headaches for three weeks. They are worst on waking and she has been vomiting before breakfast. Her mother has now noticed that she sees double and tilts her head when reading. She has no fever, no neck stiffness and no history of head injury.

What is the most appropriate approach?
UN3346.correct_answer: Urgent paediatric assessment for possible raised intracranial pressure

UN3346.stem: A 34-year-old man with a confirmed diagnosis of raised intracranial pressure undergoes fundoscopy as part of his assessment. Which finding would most specifically confirm papilloedema?
UN3346.correct_answer: Bilateral disc swelling with blurred margins

UN3346.stem: A 28-year-old obese woman has daily headaches that are worse in the morning and on lying down, with brief episodes of visual blurring and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT of the head is normal. Lumbar puncture shows a markedly raised opening pressure with normal CSF constituents. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 26-year-old obese woman presents with a 6-week history of daily headache worse on lying down and on coughing, with transient visual obscurations. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT head is normal. What is the most appropriate next investigation?
UN3346.correct_answer: Lumbar puncture with measurement of opening pressure

UN3346.presentation: New Focal Seizure with Mass Lesion
UN3346.stem: Imaging confirms an intracranial mass in a 60-year-old woman, and she now has her first-ever seizure, limited to jerking of one hand. Which mechanism best explains why this localised fit has occurred?
UN3346.correct_answer: Abnormal discharge from cortex irritated by the lesion

UN3346.presentation: Brain metastases with vasogenic oedema — symptomatic drug treatment
UN3346.stem: A 64-year-old woman with known non-small-cell lung cancer has a 10-day history of headache that is worse in the morning, with nausea and mild unsteadiness. She has had no seizures. Contrast CT of the head shows two metastases in the right cerebral hemisphere with extensive surrounding vasogenic oedema but no midline shift or hydrocephalus. She is alert and orientated. Which drug should be started now?

UN3442.stem: A 50-year-old man with chronic alcohol dependence is brought in confused, with unsteady gait and abnormal eye movements (ophthalmoplegia and nystagmus). What is the most appropriate immediate management?

A 55-year-old man with a long history of alcohol dependence is admitted with confusion. On examination he has nystagmus, a lateral rectus palsy and an ataxic gait. He is disorientated. No focal weakness is found. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
UN3442.correct_answer: Give parenteral thiamine urgently, before any glucose load

UN3442.stem: A 50-year-old man with chronic alcohol dependence is brought in confused. On examination he has nystagmus and a lateral rectus palsy (ophthalmoplegia) and an ataxic gait. What is the most appropriate immediate management?

A 55-year-old man with alcohol dependence is brought to the emergency department with confusion. He last drank this morning. He is ataxic, has horizontal nystagmus and cannot fully abduct either eye. His capillary glucose is 5.8 mmol/L and he has no tremor or sweating.

Which treatment should be given first?

A 52-year-old woman with long-standing heavy alcohol use is admitted with acute pancreatitis. On her second day on the ward she becomes disorientated, walks with a wide-based unsteady gait and has nystagmus with weakness of lateral gaze in both eyes. Deficiency of which vitamin should be suspected?

A 55-year-old man who is dependent on alcohol is brought to the emergency department by paramedics. He is disorientated, cannot walk without support and has nystagmus on looking to either side. His capillary glucose is normal. Wernicke encephalopathy is suspected. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
UN3442.correct_answer: Intravenous high-potency B vitamins including thiamine

UN3442.presentation: Intention Tremor and an Unsteady Gait
UN3442.stem: A patient has a tremor that worsens as the hand approaches a target, overshoots when reaching for objects, and a wide-based, unsteady gait. Which neurological structure is most likely affected?
A 55-year-old man presents with an unsteady, broad-based gait and a tremor that worsens as his finger approaches his nose on examination. Which part of the nervous system is most likely affected?

UN3477.stem: A patient has a unilateral constricted pupil (miosis), partial drooping of the upper eyelid (ptosis) and reduced sweating on that side of the face (anhidrosis). What does this triad represent, and what serious cause must be considered?
UN3477.correct_answer: Horner's syndrome — consider a Pancoast (apical lung) tumour or carotid dissection

UN3477.stem: A 55-year-old man has partial drooping of the right upper eyelid with a constricted (small) right pupil and reduced sweating over the right side of his face. The right pupil reacts normally to light, and eye movements are full. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 62-year-old smoker has shoulder and inner-arm pain with wasting of the small muscles of the hand. On the same side he has a drooping eyelid, a constricted pupil and reduced facial sweating. A chest X-ray shows an apical lung shadow. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3477.presentation: Horner's syndrome from an apical lung tumour
UN3477.stem: A 62-year-old woman who smoked for 35 years sees her GP with 3 months of severe pain in her left shoulder that spreads down the inner side of her arm to her little finger. She has noticed weakness and wasting of the small muscles of her left hand. Her left upper eyelid droops slightly and her left pupil is smaller than the right, with no difference in eye movements. What is the most likely cause?

UN3477.presentation: Neck pain, Horner syndrome and TIA — confirming carotid dissection
UN3477.stem: A 42-year-old man attends the emergency department with left-sided neck pain and headache that started after a chiropractic neck manipulation two days ago. His wife noticed that his left eyelid is drooping. This morning he had 20 minutes of right-hand weakness and difficulty finding words, which has fully resolved. On examination he has mild left ptosis and a small left pupil that reacts to light. A non-contrast CT head is normal. Which investigation will best confirm the suspected cause?
UN3477.correct_answer: CT angiography of the head and neck

UN3477.presentation: Neck pain, headache and focal deficit in a young adult — carotid dissection
UN3477.stem:
A 41-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 1 hour after her left arm and the left side of her face suddenly became weak, and she started bumping into things on her left. For 3 days she has had a constant pain in the right side of her neck spreading to her right forehead, which began after a roller-coaster ride. She has never had migraines. On examination she has weakness of the left face and arm, ignores objects on her left side, and has a slightly drooping right upper eyelid with a smaller right pupil. She is afebrile, and her blood pressure and capillary glucose are normal.

Which diagnosis best explains her presentation?

A pharmacy assistant attends a first-aid training session and is taught a simple community tool to help recognise a possible stroke and call 999 quickly. Which of the following is one of the features this tool asks people to check?
UN3477.correct_answer: Drooping of one side of the face

UN3477.stem: A 40-year-old man has a firm, painless lump within his upper eyelid that has been present and unchanged for six weeks. There is no redness or tenderness. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3528.stem: An overweight middle-aged man has loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, unrefreshing sleep and marked daytime sleepiness (a high Epworth score). What is the most appropriate investigation and first-line treatment if confirmed?
UN3528.correct_answer: Sleep study, then CPAP (with weight loss) if confirmed moderate-to-severe

UN3528.presentation: Suspected obstructive sleep apnoea — first diagnostic test
UN3528.stem: A 55-year-old man is seen in a sleep clinic with loud snoring, witnessed pauses in his breathing, unrefreshing sleep and daytime sleepiness. His Epworth Sleepiness Scale score is 14 and his BMI is 36 kg/m². He has no heart failure or chronic lung disease, and all sleep diagnostic services are available locally. Which is the most appropriate first diagnostic test?

UN3528.presentation: Moderate obstructive sleep apnoea syndrome — DVLA advice
UN3528.stem: A 49-year-old man who holds a car licence only has a sleep study showing moderate obstructive sleep apnoea, with an apnoea–hypopnoea index of 22 events per hour. He has excessive daytime sleepiness and recently nearly fell asleep while waiting at traffic lights. Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) treatment is being arranged. He asks what this means for his driving. What is the most appropriate advice?
UN3528.correct_answer: He must stop driving now and must notify the DVLA himself

UN3528.stem: A 60-year-old woman has brief episodes of rotational vertigo lasting under a minute, triggered by rolling over in bed or looking up. The Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre reproduces transient vertigo with rotatory nystagmus. What is the most appropriate treatment?

A young adult with a family history of kidney failure has hypertension, bilateral flank masses and episodes of visible haematuria. Ultrasound shows multiple bilateral renal cysts. What is the most likely diagnosis and an important associated risk?

A 30-year-old woman has recurrent episodes of sudden breathlessness with audible inspiratory noise from the throat. Episodes start and stop abruptly, her oxygen saturations stay normal throughout, and trials of high-dose inhaled and oral steroids have not helped. What is the most likely diagnosis?
A young adult has fever, headache, confusion and a witnessed seizure, with altered behaviour but no purpuric rash. What is the most appropriate immediate treatment while investigations proceed?

A 28-year-old obese woman has daily headaches that are worse in the morning and on lying down, with brief episodes of visual blurring and pulsatile tinnitus. Fundoscopy shows bilateral papilloedema. CT of the head is normal. Lumbar puncture shows a markedly raised opening pressure with normal CSF constituents. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3653.stem: A 40-year-old develops involuntary, jerky, dance-like movements (chorea), alongside progressive cognitive decline and behavioural/psychiatric changes. His father had a similar illness that began at a slightly older age. What is the most likely diagnosis and inheritance pattern?

A 38-year-old man sees his GP. His father, now 58, was recently diagnosed with Huntington disease after developing involuntary jerky movements and personality change. The man has two young children and wants to understand how the condition is passed on in families. Which statement about its inheritance is accurate?
UN3653.correct_answer: It is autosomal dominant, so a child of an affected parent has a 1 in 2 chance of inheriting it

UN3653.stem: A 29-year-old woman at her 12-week antenatal appointment says her husband, aged 38, has just been diagnosed with Huntington disease by the neurology team after developing jerky movements and irritability. She is not affected and has no family history. She asks the midwife what the chance is that the baby has inherited the faulty gene from him. What is the approximate risk?
A 41-year-old man whose mother has Huntington disease asks about how the condition is inherited. What type of inheritance does Huntington disease typically follow?

A 47-year-old woman is brought to the memory clinic by her husband. Over two years she has become irritable and disorganised, and she now has restless, flowing, purposeless movements of her face and hands that she seems unaware of. Her mother died in a nursing home in her sixties after a similar illness. Which pattern of inheritance does the most likely condition follow?

UN3653.presentation: Huntington disease — drug for troublesome chorea
UN3653.stem: A 46-year-old man with genetically confirmed Huntington disease is seen in the neurology clinic. Over the past year his involuntary movements have become worse, and he now spills drinks and has fallen twice. His mood is good, he has no history of depression and he has no suicidal thoughts. Liver function is normal. The team decides to start medication for his chorea. Which drug is most appropriate?

UN3653.presentation: Jerky movements after a sore throat
UN3653.stem:
A 9-year-old girl is brought to her GP because over a fortnight she has become clumsy, drops her pencil and spills drinks. Her teacher has noticed grimacing and brief, irregular jerky movements of her hands and face that disappear when she sleeps, and she has been unusually tearful. Five weeks ago she had a sore throat that was not treated. She has no fever, joint pain or rash.

Which is the most likely cause of her movements?

An 83-year-old woman has had slowly worsening memory problems over the past three years. She remains alert with no fluctuation in her level of consciousness, and her son reports she now struggles to manage her bills and medications. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3656.stem: A patient describes an irresistible urge to move the legs, often with an unpleasant crawling sensation, that is worse in the evening and at rest and is relieved by moving around. What is the most likely diagnosis and a key reversible factor to check?
UN3656.correct_answer: Restless legs syndrome — check ferritin, as iron deficiency is a common, treatable contributor

UN3656.presentation: Bilateral Leg Weakness With Urinary Symptoms
UN3656.stem: New urinary difficulty, numbness around the perineum and worsening weakness and numbness in both legs develop in a 36-year-old woman. What is the most important diagnosis to consider?

UN3656.presentation: Back Pain With New Bladder and Leg Symptoms
UN3656.stem: A patient with a history of chronic low back pain presents with a new inability to pass urine, numbness around the perineum, and weakness affecting both legs. What is the most likely diagnosis?

A 44-year-old man attends the emergency department with two days of severe low back pain radiating down both legs. He has not passed urine since the morning but does not feel the urge to. Examination shows reduced pinprick sensation over the perineum, around the anus, over the buttocks and on the inner thighs. Which term best describes this sensory finding?

A 26-year-old woman develops progressive difficulty walking upstairs over several days, two weeks after an episode of diarrhoea. On examination she has symmetrical weakness in both legs with absent reflexes. What is the most likely diagnosis?

UN3656.presentation: Myeloma with suspected spinal cord compression — imaging
UN3656.stem: A 71-year-old man with multiple myeloma is an inpatient on the haematology ward. Over 5 days he has developed worsening mid-thoracic back pain that is worse when lying flat, and since yesterday both legs have felt heavy. Examination shows power 4/5 in both legs and brisk knee and ankle reflexes. Which investigation is most appropriate?
UN3656.correct_answer: MRI of the whole spine within 24 hours

UN3656.stem: A 45-year-old man presents with progressive ascending weakness of both legs over 4 days, now reaching the lower trunk. There is areflexia, and he had a diarrhoeal illness 2 weeks ago. Sensation is intact. Which investigation will best confirm the diagnosis?

UN3656.presentation: Mixed Upper And Lower Motor Neurone Signs
UN3656.stem: Visible wasting, fasciculations and brisk reflexes accompany progressively worsening weakness in both legs of a 64-year-old woman. Which diagnosis is most likely?

UN3658.stem: A patient presents with sudden right-sided weakness and is found on examination to have increased muscle tone and exaggerated, brisk reflexes on the affected side. What type of lesion does this suggest?
A 75-year-old man is found to have a tremor at rest, slowness of movement and increased muscle tone. Which diagnosis is most likely?

An overweight middle-aged man has loud snoring, witnessed apnoeas, unrefreshing sleep and marked daytime sleepiness (a high Epworth score). What is the most appropriate investigation and first-line treatment if confirmed?
UN3658.correct_answer: Sleep study, then CPAP (with weight loss) if confirmed moderate-to-severe

UN3658.presentation: Suspected obstructive sleep apnoea — first diagnostic test
